newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ on top of fiscal/monetary policy mix - Birch.
newsitem.headline: NZ on top of fiscal/monetary policy mix - Birch.

text.p: New Zealand Finance Minister Bill Birch on Monday said the coalition government would continue to monitor the interaction of its monetary and fiscal policies in the service of balance and economic growth.

"The coalition has proved itself strongly aware that excessive fiscal easing would put pressure on monetary conditions, to the detriment of growth in the tradeables sector," Birch said in a speech to the SBC Warburg Investor Group in Wellington.

He said the coalition had defered for 12 months this year's $1 billion tax cut to offset extra spending and, as an additional safeguard, the Budget Policy Statement had fixed this year's new spending at NZ$950 million, $250 million lower than the $1.2 million originally earmarked.
The coalition agreement signed in December between the National and New Zealand First parties commits a total of not more than $5 billion extra spending in the three years to 1999/2000.
Birch said government expenditure was not out of hand.

"No way is expenditure out of hand. Despite extra spending in priority areas, government spending is projected to fall from 33.4 percent to 32.1 percent of GDP in the three-year term of the present coalition," he said.
